findings.title: Null check for rawTokenId is wrong and rawTokenId is never validated
findings.body: The constructor checks `grantType` twice; the second check on line 73 should be `rawTokenId`. As written, a null rawTokenId is accepted silently, and the message 'Null rawTokenId not allowed' is never produced. This is a copy-paste defect in the validation intended to guard the field.

findings.title: Parsing an encoded token ID with a colon in a legacy UUID-only id is treated inconsistently
findings.body: getTokenContextFromTokenId uses indexOf(':') and, when no colon is present, treats the whole string as raw id. But when the colon is present and the prefix length is not 6, it throws IllegalArgumentException. Any caller that passes an arbitrary or attacker-controlled token ID (e.g. from an introspection request or a Details value) can trigger an exception path; callers must handle IllegalArgumentException, and the contract is not documented or enforced consistently at call sites. Also, the grant-type lookup for unknown shortcuts can trigger factory scans on every call with attacker-supplied input, since getGrantTypeByShortcut refreshes maps on each miss.

findings.title: Cache-miss refresh performs provider lookup and map mutation on every unknown shortcut/grant
findings.body: getGrantTypeByShortcut and getShortcutByGrantType re-scan provider factories and write to ConcurrentHashMaps whenever a lookup misses. Because token IDs can be supplied by clients (for introspection/userinfo), an attacker can send arbitrary unknown grant shortcuts forcing repeated stream scans and map writes on each request. Negative results are not cached, so the cost is paid per request.

findings.title: Grant maps are non-atomic across two maps, so reads can see inconsistent state
findings.body: grantsByShortcuts and grantsToShortcuts are updated with two separate put calls, and the lookup methods read them separately. A concurrent thread can observe a shortcut present in one map but not the other, causing getShortcutByGrantType to return null and encodeTokenId to throw IllegalStateException for a valid grant. The two maps are also not kept in sync if a shortcut is reused, since the duplicate check runs only in postInit.

findings.title: UNKNOWN grant placeholder collides with a shortcut namespace and breaks duplicate validation
findings.body: The placeholder 'na' is inserted into both maps after the provider scan, so the size check at line 82 is always compared against an extra entry. If any grant factory ever declares shortcut 'na', it is silently overwritten by the placeholder rather than rejected, undermining the validation the check is meant to provide.

findings.title: Potential NullPointerException when client session context has no user session
findings.body: getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext dereferences clientSessionContext.getClientSession().getUserSession() and calls getPersistenceState and isOffline without null checks. Callers such as the token exchange and refresh paths may supply contexts where the user session is not yet attached, so token creation fails with an NPE instead of a clear error.

findings.title: Token ID encoding can throw on unknown grant and breaks token creation for grants that do not set GRANT_TYPE
findings.body: initToken now calls encodeTokenId, which throws IllegalStateException for UNKNOWN session/token types or unrecognised grant types. Grant paths that do not set Constants.GRANT_TYPE (for example the grants touched only partially, or any custom grant without a factory shortcut) will fall back to 'na' and encoding throws for unknown session types. A regression here would make access token issuance fail for existing flows instead of degrading gracefully.

findings.title: Grant type attribute is set from context.getGrantType() which is the raw form parameter
findings.body: createTokenResponse writes context.getGrantType(), which is the raw grant_type form value, into the session note. For token-exchange and other grants this value may differ from the factory id, and a missing or invalid grant_type is stored as null, which then triggers Assert/IllegalState in encoding via a null grant. The grant identifier should come from the grant factory rather than a request parameter.

findings.title: Blank line removed alongside functional change
findings.body: The diff replaces an empty line with the setAttribute call, which is harmless, but the grant type is set on sessionContext only after the note is set, while other grants set it on clientSessionCtx after attachSession. Consistency between grant implementations is lost, making it easy to miss the attribute on new grants.

findings.title: isAccessTokenId matcher has inverted logic and wrong offsets
findings.body: The matcher returns false when the grant shortcut equals the expected one (`if (items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;`), so correct token IDs fail and incorrect ones pass. The substring offset 3..5 is also wrong for the 'st+tt+gt:' format where the grant shortcut occupies chars 4..6 (index 4 to 6). Event assertions on TOKEN_ID will therefore misbehave in the integration tests.

findings.title: Negative test cannot fail properly and assertion is swallowed
findings.body: testIncorrectGrantType catches RuntimeException, which also catches the AssertionError produced by Assert.fail? No, AssertionError is not a RuntimeException, so the fail is not swallowed; however the test catches any RuntimeException including NPEs, so it passes for unrelated bugs. It should assert the specific IllegalArgumentException and message.

findings.title: Grant maps are package-private mutable fields used by tests
findings.body: grantsByShortcuts and grantsToShortcuts are package-private non-final fields, which the test mutates directly. Production code and tests share mutable internals, and the test bypasses postInit, so the test does not exercise the real initialization path.
